title: Checkout / payments
summary: Price and quantity tamper, currency, coupons, payment binding, checkout races, and CSRF on place-order.

groups.title: Amounts and coupons
groups.summary: The server, not the client, owns the price.

checks.title: Client-supplied price
checks.why: The checkout POST accepts price, total, or unit_amount from the client.
checks.validate: The charged or recorded amount is the tampered value, not the catalog price.

variants.name: Lower the unit price
variants.payload:
POST /cart/items HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"sku":"SKU-1","qty":1,"price":0.01,"unit_amount":1}
variants.expect: Read the cart and the payment intent. Price must be recomputed from SKU-1.
variants.why: A client-supplied unit price means the server trusts the price the client sends.

variants.name: Negative / zero total
variants.payload:
POST /checkout HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"total":0,"amount":-1}
variants.expect: Must refuse. A fulfilled order at 0 is the finding.
variants.why: A negative or zero total exploits sign/zero handling to pay nothing.

variants.name: Hidden integrity field
variants.payload:
POST /checkout HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"total":1,"checksum":"deadbeef","hash":"00"}
variants.expect: A client hash is not a control. Tamper it; the server must ignore it.
variants.why: A hidden price/signature field the client controls can be replayed to a cheaper value.

checks.title: Quantity, currency, extras
checks.why: Negative qty, a cheaper currency, or a skipped tax line changes what is settled.
checks.validate: The settled amount or stock movement does not match the catalog rules.

variants.name: Negative quantity
variants.payload:
POST /cart/items HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"sku":"SKU-1","qty":-1}
variants.expect: Must refuse. A credit or stock increase is the finding.
variants.why: Negative quantities can flip charges into credits.

variants.name: Currency swap
variants.payload:
POST /checkout HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"currency":"IDR","total":10}
variants.expect: Currency must be bound to the catalog/settlement context, not the client string.
variants.why: Swapping currency is parsed differently at pricing vs settlement, creating a rate mismatch.

variants.name: Drop tax / shipping
variants.payload:
POST /checkout HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"skip_tax":true,"shipping":0,"discount":999}
variants.expect: Tax, shipping, and discount must be recomputed server-side.
variants.why: Removing tax/shipping fields may change the server-computed total.

checks.title: Coupon eligibility and stacking
checks.why: A one-use or new-customer coupon applies twice, on the wrong cart, or stacks past the limit.
checks.validate: The discount that lands is one the account was not eligible for.

variants.name: Apply another user's code
variants.payload:
POST /cart/coupon HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"code":"B-UNIQUE-CODE"}
variants.expect: A personal or single-use code for B must fail for A.
variants.why: Reusing a single-use or user-bound code is a coupon-stealing primitive.

variants.name: Stack and reuse
variants.payload:
POST /cart/coupon HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"codes":["SAVE10","SAVE10","WELCOME"]}
variants.expect: Same code twice, plus a new-customer code on an old account, must not stack past the rule.
variants.why: Redeeming the same code twice or stacking codes exploits redemption state.

groups.title: Payment bind, race, CSRF
groups.summary: The paid amount is the order; two clicks are one order; checkout is not CSRF-simple.

checks.title: Payment amount and order binding
checks.why: The webhook or confirm step trusts a client amount, or applies a payment to the wrong order.
checks.validate: A cheaper payment fulfills a dearer order, or order 1001 is marked paid by 1002's intent.

variants.name: Swap order id on confirm
variants.payload:
POST /checkout/confirm HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A>
Content-Type: application/json

{"order_id":1002,"payment_intent":"pi_A"}
variants.expect: pi_A was created for 1001. Must not fulfill 1002.
variants.why: Confirming a payment against a different order id breaks the amount-to-order binding.

variants.name: Webhook amount mismatch
variants.payload: If you control a test webhook, replay a succeeded event with amount=1 against a larger order.
variants.expect: Must refuse. Do not replay live provider events against production money.
variants.why: A webhook amount that differs from the order total means settlement does not verify the charge.

checks.title: Double checkout / double spend
checks.why: Two parallel place-order requests both succeed on a single-use cart, coupon, or wallet.
checks.validate: Two orders or two deductions from one intended payment. Use your test wallet only.

variants.name: Parallel place-order
variants.payload: Capture one POST /checkout. Fire it twice at the same moment (Turbo Intruder / two Repeater tabs).
variants.expect: One success, one fail. Two fulfilled orders is the finding. Keep amounts tiny.
variants.why: Two concurrent place-order calls can both consume stock or both apply a single-use coupon.

variants.name: Coupon double redeem
variants.payload: Apply a single-use code, then parallel-confirm two checkouts that both carry it.
variants.expect: The code must be consumed atomically.
variants.why: Concurrent redeems race the redemption flag.

checks.title: CSRF on place-order
checks.why: A cross-site POST places an order on the victim's saved instrument.
checks.validate: A cross-origin form creates a real order. Use a test catalog item.

variants.name: Cross-site place-order
variants.payload:
<form action="https://www.example.com/checkout" method="POST">
  <input name="sku" value="SKU-1">
  <input name="qty" value="1">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit()</script>
variants.expect: Must fail without a valid CSRF token / step-up. Impact is a created order, not a 200.
variants.why: A cross-site order placed in a victim's session is the CSRF impact.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/checkout HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example
Cookie: session=<victim>

{"sku":"SKU-1","qty":1}
variants.expect: Must not create an order.
variants.why: A simple-request JSON order can be CSRF'd unless a token is enforced.

checks.title: Server-side workflow states mapped
checks.why: Every business-logic finding is a state the server should not allow — the map of states and transitions is the oracle.
checks.validate: A written state machine per workflow (states, legal transitions, guards, side effects) confirmed with the owner.

variants.name: State inventory
variants.payload: From docs, UI behavior, and owner confirmation, write each workflow as: states → allowed transitions → guards (who/when) → irreversible effects.
variants.expect: Owner-confirmed map; every later probe cites the transition it attacks.
variants.why: The oracle precedes the attack.

variants.name: Effect ledger
variants.payload: For each transition, list side effects (emails, charges, inventory, permissions) and whether reversible.
variants.expect: Effects marked reversible/irreversible — irreversible ones get the strictest probes.
variants.why: Irreversibility defines the blast radius.

variants.name: Hidden states
variants.payload: Probe for states the UI never shows (draft, pending-review, soft-deleted) via id fields and API responses.
variants.expect: Hidden states mapped — they often carry weaker guards.
variants.why: Dark states have dark policies.

checks.title: Mandatory steps cannot be skipped
checks.why: Calling step 4 directly (checkout without payment, publish without review) bypasses every check living in steps 1-3.
checks.validate: Every step validates the full prerequisite chain server-side; direct calls to later steps fail closed.

variants.name: Deep-link step call
variants.payload: Identify the workflow API endpoints per step; call the final step directly on a fresh object with no prior steps.
variants.expect: Refused — prerequisite chain verified server-side, not by UI flow.
variants.why: The classic: one request, zero steps.

variants.name: Out-of-shape step
variants.payload: Call step N with the payload shape of step N-1 (or empty).
variants.expect: Rejected with a state error; no partial advancement.
variants.why: Wrong-shape acceptance reveals absent guards.

variants.name: Step result forgery
variants.payload: Submit step N carrying client-attested proof of step N-1 (paid=true, verified=true fields).
variants.expect: Server re-derives prerequisites from authoritative state; client claims ignored.
variants.why: Client-attested state is storytelling.

checks.title: Out-of-order transitions rejected
checks.why: State machines enforce order; APIs without order checks accept transitions that make no sense and break invariants.
checks.validate: Only legal transitions per the state map succeed; illegal ones are refused with clear state errors.

variants.name: Reverse walk
variants.payload: Execute the workflow backwards: cancel after completion, unapprove after payout, reopen after close.
variants.expect: Each illegal transition refused; no resurrection of terminal states.
variants.why: Running the film backwards finds missing guards.

variants.name: Sibling hop
variants.payload: From one state, fire transitions only legal from a different state.
variants.expect: Refused — transition legality bound to current state.
variants.why: Transitions have addresses; test the wrong ones.

variants.name: Terminal immutability
variants.payload: On terminal states (completed, refunded, deleted), attempt every mutating operation.
variants.expect: Terminal is terminal — full refusal set verified.
variants.why: Dead objects must not write.

checks.title: Completed actions cannot be replayed
checks.why: Replaying a completed action (approval, redemption, vote) double-spends its effect even without a race.
checks.validate: One-time actions are single-use with server-side consumption; replay returns the original result or a clear error.

variants.name: Sequential replay
variants.payload: Complete a one-time action; immediately repeat the identical request.
variants.expect: Second call fails (or is idempotent by design) — never a second effect.
variants.why: The polite version before the racing version.

variants.name: Cross-session replay
variants.payload: Replay the action from a second session/context of the same account.
variants.expect: Still single-use — consumption is server-global, not per-session.
variants.why: Session boundaries do not reset one-time semantics.

variants.name: Modified replay
variants.payload: Replay with minor variations (same id, different amount or target).
variants.expect: Variations treated as new requests requiring full validation — no id-based shortcut.
variants.why: Idempotency keys must bind the whole action.

checks.title: Workflow tokens bound to account and object
checks.why: Action tokens (approve links, quote ids, edit keys) used on other objects or accounts are privilege by confusion.
checks.validate: Every workflow token is bound to exactly one account, object, action, and expiry; cross-use is refused.

variants.name: Token transplant
variants.payload: Take a valid token for object A (yours); present it for object B (also yours) through the same endpoint.
variants.expect: Refused — the token names its object.
variants.why: Two honest objects, one dishonest combination.

variants.name: Cross-account token
variants.payload: Capture a token from account A; use it against the same object id visible to account B.
variants.expect: Refused — account binding enforced.
variants.why: Token theft is the threat model; binding is the control.

variants.name: Expired-token replay
variants.payload: Use the token after its documented validity.
variants.expect: Refused; expiry enforced server-side.
variants.why: Token lifetime is a server decision.

checks.title: Account-state prerequisites for sensitive flows
checks.why: Unverified, suspended, closed, and recovery-pending accounts must not perform sensitive actions.
checks.validate: Sensitive flows check current account state at execution time; blocked states fail closed.

variants.name: State matrix
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: put your test account in each state (unverified, locked, closed) and attempt the sensitive flow.
variants.expect: Each blocked state refuses the flow; matrix documented.
variants.why: The matrix is the deliverable.

variants.name: Mid-flow state change
variants.payload: Start the flow healthy; owner-assisted suspend the account mid-flow; complete it.
variants.expect: Completion re-checks account state — suspended mid-flow dies.
variants.why: TOCTOU on account state.

variants.name: Backdoor state fields
variants.payload: Attempt to influence the account-state check via request fields (status, verified flags).
variants.expect: Client fields never change authoritative account state.
variants.why: State comes from the server, always.

checks.title: Time windows validated with server time
checks.why: Client clocks, timezone fields, and date parameters that influence windows (auctions, bookings, offers) are free forgery.
checks.validate: All window logic uses trusted server time; client-supplied times are advisory at most.

variants.name: Date-field forgery
variants.payload: Submit booking/auction/offer requests with date fields shifted to exploit the window (past start, after end, cross-timezone).
variants.expect: Window decisions use server time; forged dates ignored or validated.
variants.why: The client's watch is not the server's clock.

variants.name: Timezone confusion
variants.payload: Boundary cases across timezones (UTC vs local) on window open/close.
variants.expect: One authoritative timezone; boundaries unambiguous.
variants.why: Timezone bugs are logic bugs.

variants.name: Clock-skew boundary
variants.payload: Requests just inside and just outside the window boundary (measured against server responses).
variants.expect: Boundary enforced exactly; document the observed edge behavior.
variants.why: Boundaries are where money changes hands.

checks.title: Consent and disclosure decisions preserved
checks.why: Terms, risk acknowledgements, and regulatory disclosures that can be skipped or reset expose the business legally.
checks.validate: Consent states bind to the workflow version and account; they cannot be skipped, replayed away, or silently reset.

variants.name: Consent-skip probe
variants.payload: Proceed through the workflow without accepting required consents (direct API calls).
variants.expect: Refused — consent is a prerequisite like any step.
variants.why: The regulatory version of step-skipping.

variants.name: Consent reset
variants.payload: Attempt to reset/clear consent flags via profile updates or replays.
variants.expect: Consent history immutable for users; resets require the documented path.
variants.why: Rewriting history is a compliance finding.

variants.name: Version binding
variants.payload: If terms version changes mid-flow, check which version the completed action records.
variants.expect: Consent bound to a specific version; ambiguity documented.
variants.why: Which terms did they actually accept?

checks.title: Business rules verified across adjacent channels
checks.why: A fix in the web UI that misses the mobile API or batch path is no fix — adjacent channels carry the old logic.
checks.validate: Every business rule tested on the primary channel is repeated on adjacent channels (mobile, API, batch, webhook-triggered).

variants.name: Channel matrix
variants.payload: Take the three strongest findings/probes from this engagement; repeat each on every channel that reaches the same flow.
variants.expect: Same enforcement everywhere; misses documented as channel gaps.
variants.why: The remediation test, pre-written.

variants.name: Batch/backdoor channel
variants.payload: Import, bulk, and integration paths that create the same objects bypassing the interactive flow.
variants.expect: Batch paths enforce the same invariants.
variants.why: Imports are the classic rules bypass.

variants.name: Webhook-triggered path
variants.payload: Where webhooks drive workflow transitions, replay/forge webhook shapes that trigger the rule-bearing action.
variants.expect: Webhook-driven transitions validate like human-driven ones.
variants.why: Machines skip consent screens too.

checks.title: Numeric ranges and signs as business values
checks.why: Quantities, amounts, and counts carry business meaning: negative quantities move money backwards; zeros and floats break invariants.
checks.validate: Numerics validated as business values (range, sign, precision, step) not just as types.

variants.name: Sign flip
variants.payload: Negative quantity/amount on orders, transfers, refunds, and ratings (own account).
variants.expect: Rejected — negatives refused where they make no business sense.
variants.why: The oldest logic flaw: arithmetic without policy.

variants.name: Precision and overflow
variants.payload: Amounts with many decimals, huge values (1e308), NaN/Infinity strings where parsers accept them.
variants.expect: Rejected by precision/scale rules; no overflow behavior.
variants.why: Money is decimal, not float — prove it.

variants.name: Zero and step abuse
variants.payload: Zero quantities, sub-step values (0.5 seats), and boundary values ±1 of limits.
variants.expect: Business floors/ceilings enforced (minimums, lot sizes).
variants.why: Boundaries are business rules in numeric clothing.

checks.title: Currency bound to trusted price context
checks.why: Price in USD paid in JPY at face value, or item priced in context A bought in context B, is a money printer.
checks.validate: Currency and price come from the server-side catalog/quote; client-supplied currency or price is ignored.

variants.name: Currency parameter swap
variants.payload: Change currency in cart/checkout requests (own cart); observe totals and charge.
variants.expect: Totals re-derived server-side per currency; client currency ignored for pricing.
variants.why: One parameter, direct loss.

variants.name: Price-field replay
variants.payload: Capture a quoted price; change cart contents; resubmit the old price with new contents.
variants.expect: Server re-prices; stale quotes rejected or revalidated.
variants.why: Stale quotes are old news worth money.

variants.name: Cross-market confusion
variants.payload: Where markets/regions have different prices, order from market B at market A pricing via mixed parameters.
variants.expect: Market-bound pricing enforced end to end.
variants.why: Region pricing is business logic attackers arbitrage.

checks.title: Tax, fees, and discounts recalculated server-side
checks.why: Totals accepted from the client let the shopper set their own price; every derived number must be server-owned.
checks.validate: All derived amounts (tax, shipping, fees, discounts, totals) are computed server-side from authoritative inputs.

variants.name: Total tamper
variants.payload: Modify total/grand_total in the checkout request (own cart) to 1 unit.
variants.expect: Charge uses the server-computed total; client totals ignored.
variants.why: The one-field price cut.

variants.name: Discount stacking
variants.payload: Apply discount fields directly (discount=90%) or stack coupons beyond policy.
variants.expect: Server validates discount eligibility and stacking rules.
variants.why: Generosity must be server-side.

variants.name: Fee omission
variants.payload: Remove optional fee fields (shipping, handling, service fee) from the payload.
variants.expect: Fees re-derived from fulfillment data; omitted fees return.
variants.why: Free shipping by deletion.

checks.title: Coupon usage and stacking limits enforced
checks.why: Coupons without usage accounting are free money: one code, infinite redemptions, stacked discounts.
checks.validate: Coupons enforce per-user, per-code, and global limits plus stacking rules server-side.

variants.name: Redemption cap
variants.payload: Redeem a test coupon to its documented per-user cap (own account).
variants.expect: Cap enforced at exactly the limit; overage refused.
variants.why: The polite count before the racing count (see race checks).

variants.name: Stacking ladder
variants.payload: Combine the coupon with itself via different case/whitespace forms, and with other promos against policy.
variants.expect: Same-code variants deduplicated; stacking rules enforced.
variants.why: CASE variants defeat naive per-code counters.

variants.name: Expired and premature
variants.payload: Redeem before start and after expiry dates.
variants.expect: Window enforced with server time.
variants.why: Time windows are usage limits too.

checks.title: Gift cards, credits, and points protected
checks.why: Stored value is money with worse auditing — balance tamper, transfer abuse, and redemption races hit directly.
checks.validate: Balance mutations are server-authoritative, logged, and bound to identity; transfers and redemptions enforce limits.

variants.name: Balance-field tamper
variants.payload: Include balance/points fields in profile updates, redemptions, and transfers (own account).
variants.expect: Balance fields ignored — server ledger only.
variants.why: The client proposes; the ledger disposes.

variants.name: Self-transfer
variants.payload: Transfer credits to your own second account repeatedly to farm bonuses or dodge limits.
variants.expect: Self-transfers blocked or correctly accounted; bonus abuse bounded.
variants.why: Two honest accounts, one dishonest loop.

variants.name: Negative redemption
variants.payload: Redeem negative amounts (adding credit) or zero-cost conversions.
variants.expect: Signs validated as business values; negative redemption refused.
variants.why: Arithmetic direction is policy.

checks.title: Checkout bound to verified payment state
checks.why: Marking an order paid without a verified provider confirmation (or before it settles) ships free goods.
checks.validate: Order completion requires provider-verified payment state via server-side confirmation (webhook with signature or verified API check).

variants.name: Client-confirmed probe
variants.payload: Complete checkout with client-side payment-success signals (success flags, redirects) manipulated.
variants.expect: No fulfillment without server-verified payment.
variants.why: The UI is not the payment provider.

variants.name: Webhook forgery
variants.payload: Replay/forge the payment-success webhook with tampered amounts or order ids (your own order).
variants.expect: Signature verified; amounts and order binding checked; forgeries refused.
variants.why: Webhooks are unauthenticated input until signed.

variants.name: Pending-to-paid race
variants.payload: Fulfill at the moment payment is pending (before capture) if the flow allows.
variants.expect: Fulfillment gated on captured/settled state per policy.
variants.why: Pending is not paid.

checks.title: Refund and reversal limits enforced
checks.why: Refund above the paid amount, double refunds, and refunds after reversal are direct money extraction.
checks.validate: Refunds are bounded by original payment, single-execution, and lifetime limits, with reversals paired atomically.

variants.name: Over-refund
variants.payload: Request a refund larger than the payment (own test order).
variants.expect: Refused — bounded by the original amount.
variants.why: Refund is not a withdrawal.

variants.name: Double refund
variants.payload: Request the same refund twice sequentially, then via two channels if present.
variants.expect: Second refund refused; single execution per payment.
variants.why: Sequential first; the racing twin lives in race checks.

variants.name: Refund-after-use
variants.payload: Refund after consumption/fulfillment where policy forbids it.
variants.expect: Refund gated on order state per policy.
variants.why: State gates refunds too.

checks.title: Cancellation constrained after irreversible states
checks.why: Cancelling after shipment/payout reverses irreversible effects on paper while goods are gone.
checks.validate: Cancellation rules follow the state map; irreversible states refuse or route to the returns process.

variants.name: Late cancellation
variants.payload: Attempt cancellation after each irreversible milestone (payment, shipment, activation).
variants.expect: Refused per policy; only documented post-states allow it.
variants.why: The map says where the cliff is.

variants.name: Cancellation-reversal mismatch
variants.payload: Cancel one side of a two-sided transaction (cancel order but keep payout running).
variants.expect: Paired effects cancelled together; no orphaned money flows.
variants.why: Two-ledger systems cancel twice or not at all.

variants.name: Refund-via-cancel loop
variants.payload: Alternate cancel and re-order to farm refund bonuses or trials.
variants.expect: Loop abuse bounded by usage limits.
variants.why: Loops are policies repeated.

checks.title: Subscription and trial lifecycle rules
checks.why: Trials that never end, downgrades that keep features, and date tampering are entitlement theft by calendar.
checks.validate: Trials are once-per-identity with server-side dates; plan changes apply exact entitlement deltas immediately.

variants.name: Trial rebirth
variants.payload: End a trial; start another with the same account (then with a second account + same payment identity if in scope).
variants.expect: One trial per identity per policy; rebirth blocked.
variants.why: Identity is the dedup key for generosity.

variants.name: Downgrade retention
variants.payload: Downgrade from premium to free; immediately use premium features.
variants.expect: Entitlements cut at downgrade; no grace beyond policy.
variants.why: Downgrades must actually descend.

variants.name: Date-field tamper
variants.payload: Extend trial/subscription by editing date fields in requests or profile payloads.
variants.expect: Server-authoritative dates; client fields ignored.
variants.why: Calendars are server-side assets.

checks.title: Per-user and global usage limits
checks.why: Quotas on messages, exports, seats, and votes bound cost and abuse; per-request checks without accounting are theater.
checks.validate: Usage counters are server-side, per-identity, and enforced at execution with clear errors at the cap.

variants.name: Cap walk
variants.payload: Use the metered feature to its documented cap; one more.
variants.expect: Refused exactly at the cap with a clear error.
variants.why: Find the wall, cite it.

variants.name: Counter-reset hunt
variants.payload: Look for counter resets via logout, device change, cache purge, or id rotation.
variants.expect: Counters bind to identity, not sessions or devices.
variants.why: The counter must outlive the session.

variants.name: Concurrent accounting
variants.payload: Two parallel uses at the cap boundary.
variants.expect: Counter is atomic; no over-spend by interleaving (see race checks for the hammer).
variants.why: Sequential caps first; concurrency later.

checks.title: Limit reset through alternate identities blocked
checks.why: Case-variants, aliases, and throwaway identities reset naive limits; per-identity means per-human per policy.
checks.validate: Limit identity resolution covers aliases (case, plus-addressing, multiple emails, guest/auth switches) per documented policy.

variants.name: Alias spray
variants.payload: Test with your own email aliases/plus-addresses and case variants against a per-user limit.
variants.expect: Aliases canonicalized; limits bind to the canonical identity.
variants.why: user+1@example is still user@example to a good limiter.

variants.name: Guest-to-auth switch
variants.payload: Use the feature as guest, then authenticated with the same underlying identity.
variants.expect: Guest and authed usage merged per policy.
variants.why: The same human through two doors.

variants.name: Channel split
variants.payload: Use web quota, then API quota, for the same underlying resource.
variants.expect: Cross-channel accounting unified.
variants.why: Channels share the meter.

checks.title: Plan and entitlement downgrade confusion prevented
checks.why: Changing plan ids or feature flags in requests retains higher-tier features without payment — entitlement by typo.
checks.validate: Entitlements derive from server-side subscription state; plan/flag fields in client payloads change nothing.

variants.name: Plan-id swap
variants.payload: Submit plan/tier/package ids of a higher plan in downgrade or update calls (own account).
variants.expect: Server derives entitlements from its own records; ids are not upgrades.
variants.why: Naming a plan is not buying it.

variants.name: Feature-flag carryover
variants.payload: After downgrade, probe previously-premium endpoints and UI-gated functions.
variants.expect: Access cut to current-plan features exactly.
variants.why: Yesterday's features are not today's.

variants.name: Mid-cycle flip
variants.payload: Upgrade then downgrade rapidly to confuse proration or access windows.
variants.expect: Proration and access changes are atomic and audited.
variants.why: Rapid flips stress entitlement sync.

checks.title: Reservation and inventory hoarding prevented
checks.why: Unbounded holds let one account freeze inventory forever — a denial-of-service on the business itself.
checks.validate: Reservations are capped per identity, time-boxed with expiry, and released on abandonment.

variants.name: Hold cap
variants.payload: Create reservations/holds to the documented per-user cap; attempt more.
variants.expect: Capped per identity; beyond refused.
variants.why: Cap first, expiry second.

variants.name: Expiry reality
variants.payload: Hold an item; wait past the documented hold window (or owner-assisted trigger).
variants.expect: Hold released automatically; inventory returned.
variants.why: Every hold needs an hourglass.

variants.name: Abandon-release
variants.payload: Close the session mid-hold; verify release on abandonment.
variants.expect: Abandoned holds return to inventory without manual cleanup.
variants.why: Closed tabs must not own stock.

checks.title: Invitation and referral rules enforced
checks.why: Self-referral, link reuse, and inviter-editing turn growth programs into ATMs.
checks.validate: Inviter identity is server-derived; referral bonuses bound per identity; links single-use within expiry.

variants.name: Self-referral
variants.payload: Invite your own second account; complete the referral loop.
variants.expect: Self-referral detected and refused per policy.
variants.why: Two honest accounts, the classic loop.

variants.name: Inviter edit
variants.payload: Modify inviter/referrer fields after signup (own accounts).
variants.expect: Inviter immutable post-binding.
variants.why: Reattributing referrals reattributes money.

variants.name: Bonus velocity
variants.payload: Complete referrals to the documented cap; one more.
variants.expect: Caps enforced; velocity rules engaged.
variants.why: Generosity has a budget.

checks.title: Approvals bound to eligible independent reviewers
checks.why: If the requester approves their own request or picks their approver, the control is theater.
checks.validate: Approver must differ from requester, hold eligibility for the object, and be selected server-side from eligible sets.

variants.name: Self-approval
variants.payload: Request as A; approve as A.
variants.expect: Refused — independence enforced server-side.
variants.why: The direct probe.

variants.name: Approver nomination
variants.payload: Requester-nominated approver fields (approver_id in the request payload).
variants.expect: Server ignores nominations; approver chosen from eligible set.
variants.why: Choosing your own judge.

variants.name: Ineligible approver
variants.payload: Route approval to a role/account without object eligibility.
variants.expect: Eligibility verified at approval execution, not display.
variants.why: Title without jurisdiction.

checks.title: Maker-checker separation survives reassignment
checks.why: Reassigning ownership mid-approval can put both sides of the control in one pair of hands.
checks.validate: Reassignment preserves separation: a maker cannot become checker on their own request; audit records both sides.

variants.name: Reassign-to-self
variants.payload: Reassign the request to yourself (or your alias) after submitting.
variants.expect: Refused; maker identity pinned at creation.
variants.why: The subtlest path to self-approval.

variants.name: Swap dance
variants.payload: A submits, B approves; attempt to make B the maker of a modification that A then approves for the same effect.
variants.expect: Modified requests re-enter maker-checker as new work.
variants.why: Modifications are new requests.

variants.name: Resign-approve
variants.payload: If makers can cancel/withdraw, attempt withdraw-then-approve chains.
variants.expect: Withdrawn requests are dead; no zombie approvals.
variants.why: Withdrawal is not a hallway pass.

checks.title: Client-side integrity fields not trusted
checks.why: Hidden hashes, signatures, totals, and checksums computed in the browser protect only honest users.
checks.validate: Integrity values are recomputed server-side or signed with server-held keys; client values are never authoritative.

variants.name: Field-strip test
variants.payload: Remove integrity fields (hash, sig, mac) from requests; observe acceptance.
variants.expect: Server recomputes or rejects — absence is not success.
variants.why: Optional integrity is decorative.

variants.name: Value tamper
variants.payload: Modify the protected payload and re-submit the old integrity value (and vice versa).
variants.expect: Mismatch rejected; integrity covers the exact bytes.
variants.why: The signature must care about the content.

variants.name: Algorithm inspection
variants.payload: Reverse the client-side integrity computation from the bundle.
variants.expect: Client-computed values treated as hints only; findings assume attacker recomputation.
variants.why: If the browser can compute it, so can anyone.

checks.title: Search and notification abuse detected
checks.why: Search, contact, and messaging features double as scraping, spam, and harassment infrastructure.
checks.validate: High-reach features carry abuse controls: rate limits, recipient caps, content filters, and enumeration resistance.

variants.name: Enumeration resistance
variants.payload: Search for your own account as a needle (canary strings) via wildcard/prefix; measure what an attacker could enumerate.
variants.expect: Results bounded; enumeration cost documented; no silent full-dump.
variants.why: Search that returns everyone is a database leak.

variants.name: Recipient flood shape
variants.payload: Messaging/contact features: target counts, send velocity on your own accounts.
variants.expect: Per-recipient and velocity caps engaged per policy.
variants.why: Spam is a business-logic abuse with a budget.

variants.name: Content-filter bypass
variants.payload: Benign canary variants of filtered content shapes (spacing, homoglyphs) in your own messages.
variants.expect: Filters resist trivial obfuscation; findings cite the specific bypass.
variants.why: Test with canaries, never real abuse.

checks.title: Tenant-specific business invariants enforced
checks.why: Cross-tenant plans, catalogs, discounts, and workflows mixing is data corruption with compliance consequences.
checks.validate: Business objects cannot mix tenants: plan, catalog, pricing, and workflow references are tenant-bound.

variants.name: Cross-tenant composition
variants.payload: Build a cart/request referencing objects from two tenants you hold.
variants.expect: Refused — composition is tenant-pure.
variants.why: The shopping-cart border check.

variants.name: Tenant plan confusion
variants.payload: Apply tenant-1 plan/pricing to tenant-2 purchases via plan fields.
variants.expect: Plans are tenant-scoped; cross-application refused.
variants.why: B2B pricing is per-contract.

variants.name: Workflow cross-tenant
variants.payload: Trigger tenant-1 workflow steps on tenant-2 objects.
variants.expect: Workflow and object tenants must match at every step.
variants.why: Approval chains stay in-house.

checks.title: Async callbacks bound to original transactions
checks.why: Webhooks and status callbacks that update another transaction or replay are privilege: the caller writes your ledger.
checks.validate: Callbacks are signature-verified and bound to the exact transaction id/amount; replay and cross-binding refused.

variants.name: Cross-binding attempt
variants.payload: Replay a valid callback shape for transaction A against transaction B (both yours).
variants.expect: Refused — the callback names its transaction.
variants.why: The honest version of the attack.

variants.name: Amount swap
variants.payload: Valid callback with modified amount/status fields.
variants.expect: Signature fails; field tamper detected.
variants.why: Amount lives inside the signature.

variants.name: Replay window
variants.payload: Replay the valid callback within and beyond the documented window.
variants.expect: Single-use or timestamp-bounded per policy.
variants.why: Old news must stop being news.

checks.title: Async jobs within current account and object state
checks.why: Queued work executes later with worker authority — account suspended or object deleted by then?
checks.validate: Jobs re-validate account state, object existence, and permissions at execution time.

variants.name: State-change-during-queue
variants.payload: Enqueue a job; owner-assisted suspend the account or delete the object; let the job run.
variants.expect: Job aborts on state re-validation; no post-suspension effects.
variants.why: The worker wakes up in a changed world.

variants.name: Permission-change-during-queue
variants.payload: Lose the underlying permission after enqueue; fetch results.
variants.expect: Results withheld; job re-authorized before output.
variants.why: Jobs inherit current authority, not old.

variants.name: Object-mutation race
variants.payload: Enqueue; modify the object before execution.
variants.expect: Job operates on validated current state or aborts; no stale-writes.
variants.why: Workers must read fresh truth.

checks.title: Duplicate effects across retries prevented
checks.why: Networks retry; each retry without idempotency duplicates orders, grants, and messages.
checks.validate: Retry-safe design (idempotency keys, dedup windows, or naturally idempotent operations) on every mutating flow.

variants.name: Exact retry
variants.payload: Send the identical create twice sequentially (client-retry shape).
variants.expect: One effect; duplicate detected or idempotent response returned.
variants.why: The honest retry, no race needed.

variants.name: Key-free duplicate
variants.payload: Where idempotency keys are optional, retry without them.
variants.expect: Server dedups by business identity anyway (or the gap is the finding).
variants.why: Optional keys are missing keys.

variants.name: Multi-tab duplicate
variants.payload: Submit the same action from two tabs of the same session seconds apart.
variants.expect: Duplicate suppressed; one canonical result.
variants.why: Real users do this by accident daily.

groups.title: Races on value and one-time semantics

checks.title: Duplicate redemption of single-use value
checks.why: N parallel requests each pass the not-yet-redeemed check before any commits — one coupon, N discounts.
checks.validate: Single-use consumption is atomic (row lock, unique constraint, or compare-and-set); parallel redemption yields exactly one success.

variants.name: Last-byte sync
variants.payload: In Burp Repeater, send the same redemption in a parallel group of 4-8 with single-packet/last-byte release.
variants.expect: Exactly one succeeds; the rest get consumed/refused — never two successes.
variants.why: Synchronized release is the whole technique; keep groups small.

variants.name: Two-identity check
variants.payload: Race the same code across two of your own accounts if per-user limits differ from global.
variants.expect: Global counter still exact — account separation must not split the counter.
variants.why: Limits have scopes; races find the seams.

variants.name: Redeem-and-spend chain
variants.payload: After a successful race attempt, spend/transfer what succeeded; verify consistency of the ledger.
variants.expect: Ledger consistent; no phantom balances survive reconciliation.
variants.why: Follow the money after the race, not just the status codes.

checks.title: Inventory double allocation under concurrency
checks.why: Parallel purchases of the last unit each see stock=1 and both ship — inventory is money in storage.
checks.validate: Stock decrements are atomic; parallel allocation of the last unit succeeds exactly once.

variants.name: Last-unit race
variants.payload: Set stock to 1 (your own test inventory or sandbox item); race 4-6 parallel purchases.
variants.expect: One allocation; the rest fail with out-of-stock — never negative or double stock.
variants.why: The textbook TOCTOU, demonstrated safely on your own item.

variants.name: Cart-plus-direct
variants.payload: Race an add-to-cart path against a direct purchase path for the same last unit.
variants.expect: Different paths share one atomic counter.
variants.why: Two doors, one inventory.

variants.name: Oversell arithmetic
variants.payload: After races, inspect reported stock and sold counts for consistency.
variants.expect: Stock >= 0 at all times; sold <= allocated; any negative is the finding.
variants.why: The numbers after the race are the evidence.

checks.title: Balance and quota checks enforced atomically
checks.why: Check-then-act on balances lets parallel debits each pass a stale check — the account spends money twice.
checks.validate: Debits/credits are atomic against current balance (locking or compare-and-set); concurrent debits cannot overdraw.

variants.name: Parallel debit
variants.payload: With a small balance you hold, race 4-6 debits that each individually fit the balance.
variants.expect: Exactly the affordable number succeed; balance never negative.
variants.why: Classic concurrent-overdraw, on your own funds.

variants.name: Debit-credit interleave
variants.payload: Race debits against a credit/top-up in flight.
variants.expect: Final balance consistent with serialized order; no lost updates (write-write conflict handled).
variants.why: Lost-update is the quieter sibling of overdraft.

variants.name: Quota parity
variants.payload: Repeat with usage quotas (messages, exports) if present.
variants.expect: Same atomicity for counts, not just currency.
variants.why: Quotas are balances with worse PR.

checks.title: One-time tokens consumed atomically
checks.why: Racing an OTP/reset/invitation token before consumption multiplies a single-use credential into several.
checks.validate: Token consumption is atomic; parallel redemption yields exactly one outcome.

variants.name: OTP parallel verify
variants.payload: Race the same OTP submission in parallel at the verify endpoint (own account).
variants.expect: One verification succeeds; others refused after consumption.
variants.why: The code is single-use — prove it under race.

variants.name: Reset-token races
variants.payload: Race password-reset token usage (reset + login in quick succession, parallel where possible).
variants.expect: One reset; parallel reuse refused; sessions from the old token invalidated.
variants.why: Reset races are account-takeover races.

variants.name: Invite-accept race
variants.payload: Race invitation acceptance from two sessions (two of your accounts where policy allows).
variants.expect: One acceptance binds; the loser gets a clean expiry error.
variants.why: Invitations mint membership — atomically.

groups.title: Races on state, workflow, and delivery

checks.title: Authorization and state in one atomic operation
checks.why: Permissions checked, then state changes, then the action runs — an interleaved permission revocation lands in the gap.
checks.validate: Authorization decisions and the protected mutation commit atomically; revocation between check and use is impossible.

variants.name: Revoke-between
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: fire a privileged action; revoke the permission at the same moment (parallel group with the revoke request if an API exists).
variants.expect: Action either completes-before or fails-after; never completes-after revocation.
variants.why: The TOCTOU definition, staged politely.

variants.name: Object-state flip
variants.payload: Race a state transition (lock/close) against an action on the same object.
variants.expect: No post-transition effects; interleavings fail closed.
variants.why: State races are authorization races with calendars.

variants.name: Checker-version note
variants.payload: Note the enforcement mechanism if visible (optimistic concurrency, row versions).
variants.expect: Mechanism documented; absence correlated with observed races.
variants.why: Explaining the fix earns the finding respect.

checks.title: Workflow transitions with concurrency control
checks.why: Parallel transitions on one workflow instance create impossible states — approved and rejected at once.
checks.validate: Workflow transitions serialize (optimistic locking or pessimistic locks); impossible states never persist.

variants.name: Approve-reject race
variants.payload: Race approve and reject of the same request from two eligible sessions (your accounts).
variants.expect: Exactly one transition lands; the other gets a state conflict; final state consistent.
variants.why: Two honest reviewers, one request, one truth.

variants.name: Same-transition storm
variants.payload: Race identical transitions (approve x4).
variants.expect: One effect; the rest idempotent-refused — no multiplied side effects (emails, notifications).
variants.why: Duplicate approvals spam and double-count.

variants.name: Cross-node split
variants.payload: If multi-region, race transitions via two regional endpoints.
variants.expect: Global serialization; regions cannot land conflicting states.
variants.why: Geography is not a locking strategy.

checks.title: Idempotency keys bound atomically
checks.why: Two different requests racing under one idempotency key, or one request under two keys, defeats the whole contract.
checks.validate: Key binding is atomic: first writer wins; same key+payload replays return the stored result; mismatches error.

variants.name: Key collision race
variants.payload: Race two different payloads under the same idempotency key.
variants.expect: One wins; the other gets a key-conflict error — never both execute.
variants.why: The race that breaks the race protector.

variants.name: Same-payload parallel
variants.payload: Race identical requests under the same key.
variants.expect: One execution; all callers get the same response.
variants.why: Retry storms are this test in the wild.

variants.name: Key-rotation trick
variants.payload: Retry a failed request with a fresh key after partial completion.
variants.expect: Partial states cleaned up or refused; new keys do not resurrect dead operations.
variants.why: Fresh keys are not time machines.

checks.title: File-processing and publish races
checks.why: Replace a file while validation/scanning runs and the published artifact never saw the checks — TOCTOU on content.
checks.validate: Publish/serve uses the exact validated artifact version (immutable refs, hash checks, or copy-before-validate).

variants.name: Swap-during-scan
variants.payload: Upload benign file; race the replace/overwrite request against the processing-complete window (your own file).
variants.expect: Published content is the validated version; swap never bypasses checks.
variants.why: The scan guards bytes that already left.

variants.name: Publish-vs-delete
variants.payload: Race publish against deletion of the underlying object.
variants.expect: No publish of dead content; no zombie references; consistent state either way.
variants.why: Lifecycle races corrupt catalogs.

variants.name: Hash-verification probe
variants.payload: Where artifacts carry hashes/version ids, verify served content matches its recorded digest after the race attempts.
variants.expect: Digests match; any mismatch is a direct finding.
variants.why: The digest is the referee.

checks.title: Partial object construction races
checks.why: Parallel creates that each partially initialize produce objects readable before complete — or with conflicting halves.
checks.validate: Object creation is atomic: parallel creates yield independent complete objects; partial states never visible.

variants.name: Create-read interleave
variants.payload: Race object creation against immediate reads (fresh session reading the new id).
variants.expect: Readers see complete objects or 404 — never half-built records.
variants.why: The half-born user is a half-broken feature.

variants.name: Duplicate-create race
variants.payload: Race identical creates with the same business key (email, username you own).
variants.expect: Exactly one wins; uniqueness enforced under race.
variants.why: Unique constraints are race controls — prove it.

variants.name: Step-chain create
variants.payload: On multi-step creation flows, race later steps before earlier complete.
variants.expect: Later steps wait or fail; no shortcut to complete state.
variants.why: Wizards are workflows; races skip steps too.

checks.title: Synchronized race delivery without flooding
checks.why: A race you cannot deliver cleanly tests nothing: one synchronized packet beats a hundred flailing requests.
checks.validate: Tests use minimal synchronized bursts (last-byte release, single packet) with strict request caps and cleanup.

variants.name: Single-packet setup
variants.payload: Use Repeater group send with last-byte sync (or a 2-3 request script with a shared barrier) for every race test.
variants.expect: Requests land within one processing window; caps documented per test.
variants.why: Technique, not volume — four synchronized beats forty sprayed.

variants.name: Barrier script
variants.payload: For HTTP/2 targets, a tiny script sends streams with simultaneous END_STREAM; keep total requests <= 10.
variants.expect: Delivery verified by server timestamps/log correlation where owner-assisted.
variants.why: HTTP/2 multiplexing is the modern last-byte.

variants.name: Cleanup discipline
variants.payload: After each race: verify state, undo/complete test objects, and record final counts.
variants.expect: No residue; repeated runs give consistent results.
variants.why: Repeatable races are reportable races.

checks.title: Race remediation across adjacent paths
checks.why: The fixed endpoint keeps its lock; the mobile twin, batch importer, and webhook path never got it.
checks.validate: Concurrency controls verified on every path that reaches the same state: web, API, mobile, batch, webhooks.

variants.name: Path matrix rerun
variants.payload: Repeat your two strongest races on every adjacent path that mutates the same value.
variants.expect: Same atomicity everywhere; weak twins documented as findings.
variants.why: Remediation testing, pre-staged.

variants.name: Webhook-vs-user race
variants.payload: Race a user-driven mutation against the webhook-driven mutation of the same object (own data).
variants.expect: Both paths serialize against each other; no split-brain state.
variants.why: Machine and human paths share one truth.

variants.name: Retry-vs-retry
variants.payload: Race client-retry patterns on two channels simultaneously.
variants.expect: Idempotency holds under cross-channel retries.
variants.why: Real traffic retries from everywhere.
